しあわせ そう な ふたり — Two people who look happy
You say how things look (～そう: おいしそう, ふりそう), what seems to be happening (～よう です / ～みたい) and what you’ve heard (～そう です, ～らしい); and you review the unit.
they say that, I hear that
It looks like it’s going to rain.
According to the forecast, it will be clear tomorrow.
Apparently Kenji isn’t good at speeches.
To say how something LOOKS from its appearance: stem + そう (おいしそう, たのしそう, ふりそう).
To pass on information you’ve heard: plain form + そう です (はれる そう です).
To draw a conclusion from evidence: ～よう です / ～みたい です.
To use ～らしい (I hear that / typical of).
To review the unit: the potential, ～たら, giving and receiving, ～ば and ～と.
17 May, ten in the morning. Sakura and her mother, Haruka, are waiting in front of Madrid town hall. Sakura has her camera ready.
Mummy, the sky is dark. It looks like it’s going to rain.
No problem. According to the forecast, it clears up from the afternoon.
Ah, Mihai’s here! …He’s pale. He looks like he’s feeling ill.
It’s not that he’s ill; it seems he’s nervous. His hands are trembling too.
And Daddy? Is Daddy nervous too?
Daddy is holding the rings, so it seems even harder for him. Since this morning he’s checked his pocket I don’t know how many times.
Ah! Ana! …Wow, how beautiful she is! There’s a blue flower on the bodice of her dress.
And she has the white hairpin in her hair. They say it’s the hairpin of Mrs Fumiko and her sister’s mother.
Is Ana crying? …No, she’s laughing. But she looks about to cry.
Sakura, take a photo of them. Of their happiest faces.
Leave it to me! Today I’ll take the best photo.
at, in; “ni yoru to” = according to
sohh: a long “o”. おいしそう = o-i-shi-soh. Said with wide eyes, it sounds very natural.
kan-pai: the “n” before “p” sounds almost like “m”: “kampai”.
o-me-de-toh go-za-i-mas: a long “o” in とう, the final “u” silent.
When you SEE something and say what impression it gives you. Add そう to the stem of the word:
looks like it’s going to rain
Exceptions: いい → よさそう (looks good), ない → なさそう. And with きれい and かわいい you DON’T use そう: you can already see they’re beautiful.
Before a noun: ～そう な: おいしそう な ケーキ (a delicious-looking cake).
2. ～そう です: “they say that” (I heard)
Careful, same syllable, different meaning! The PLAIN form (dictionary, ～た, ～ない) + そう です = you pass on information you’ve heard or read:
They say it will be clear tomorrow.
According to the forecast, it will rain.
They say it’s Mrs Fumiko’s mother’s hairpin.
When you draw a conclusion from evidence (what you see, hear or feel). Plain form + よう です (formal) or みたい (casual):
His hands are trembling. He seems to be nervous.
There’s nobody here. It looks like everyone has gone home.
With nouns: ～の よう です / ～みたい です: ゆめ の よう です = it’s like a dream. ゆめ みたい! (casual)
～らしい has two meanings: 1) “I hear that”: ケンジさん は スピーチ が にがて らしい. 2) “typical of”: おとうさん らしい = just like Dad.
“They say it will rain tomorrow.” (I heard)
The two of them look very happy.

さくら が みた けっこんしき — The wedding as Sakura saw it
Inside, the town hall was smaller and quieter than Sakura had expected.
Sakura sat in the front row, holding her camera tightly.
Next to her sat Carmen and Elena. Both were already holding handkerchiefs and looked about to cry.
In the row behind, Mrs Suzuki and Mrs Fumiko were holding hands.
The music began and Ana came in on her father’s arm.
The white dress, it seems, had belonged to her grandmother, Rosario. On the bodice was the blue flower, and in her hair the white hairpin.
Carmen and Elena looked at each other and smiled. That flower was their secret.
When Mihai saw Ana, he froze. His mouth was slightly open.
Sakura took a photo of him right then. When she looked at it later, it was a very funny face.
The ceremony began. The judge asked something in Spanish.
Sakura didn’t understand Spanish. But her mother explained in a whisper.
“She says she’s asking him if he wants to marry Ana.”
The town hall went silent. Then everyone burst out laughing.
It seems that Mihai, in his nerves, had answered in Japanese. He went bright red and said it again: “¡Sí, quiero!”
Next were the rings. Daddy put his hand in his pocket.
Daddy’s face suddenly went pale. It looked as if the rings weren’t there.
Right pocket. Left pocket. Breast pocket. Sakura couldn’t breathe.
And then, from the back pocket of his trousers, out came the little box.
Daddy let out a long breath and handed over the rings. Mummy sighed: “That’s your father all over.”
With trembling hands, Mihai put the ring on Ana’s finger. This time it went on without any trouble.
The reception was in the garden of Daddy’s restaurant. The sky had already cleared. Just as the forecast had said.
Lots of red lanterns hung in the trees. On the table stood rows of sarmale, paella and ramen.
The Spaniards tasted the sarmale and said: “More!”. The Romanians tasted the paella and said: “More!”
And when they ate the ramen, nobody said anything at all. They say it was so good they were lost for words.
Daddy gave a speech. It seems he isn’t very good at speeches. The hand holding the paper was trembling.
“These two met eating ramen at my restaurant. If it weren’t for the ramen, maybe today would never have happened.”
“So today I think I’m allowed to boast a little.” Everyone laughed and applauded.
As evening fell, Mihai put on a Romanian hora. Elena took Carmen’s hand.
Carmen took Sakura’s hand. Sakura took Daddy’s hand, and Daddy took Mummy’s.
Mrs Suzuki danced holding Tama in her arms, together with Mrs Fumiko. Both were laughing like young girls.
At the end a big circle formed: Spaniards, Romanians, Japanese and one cat.
That night, at the hotel, Sakura looked at the photos and wrote in her notebook.
“Today I saw a wedding for the first time. Even though I didn’t understand the words, I understood what everyone was feeling.”
“The best photo is the one where Mihai and Ana are laughing. They both looked very happy.”
“If one day I have someone special too, I want to laugh with a face like that.”
From the next bed, Mummy secretly read the notebook and smiled. Outside, the Madrid night seemed never to end.
The next morning, Sakura enlarged the best photo and gave it to Mihai and Ana.
On the back she had written, in hiragana: “Keep these faces all your lives. From Sakura.”
Ana held the photo to her chest and once again looked about to cry.

Text to read: Mihai’s message after the wedding
The next day, Mihai writes to all the Japanese guests.
Dear all, thank you from the bottom of my heart for coming yesterday.
I think I’ll never be able to forget saying “hai” at the town hall.
When I look at the photos Sakura took for us, I burst out laughing all over again.
If it weren’t for Kenji, we could never have met. I want to give Kenji the biggest thank-you.
Now it’s our turn to do something for you.
